title: EU Residency Authorization Switchboard for Route Selection and Tiered Fallbacks
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Summary: Implement an 'Authorization Switchboard' service that centralizes per-request residency and jurisdiction checks, enforces EU-only (customer-configured) routing, and selects an appropriate serving tier and model-variant fallback chain when preferred routes are unavailable. The switchboard sits as a policy decision layer in front of the smart router and must be fast (<=2ms median decision latency), auditable, and configurable per-account/tenant.

Background & motivation: Current routing logic is spread across multiple components (tenant metadata, route heuristics, and fallback selectors), which has led to edge cases where EU-data restrictions were not consistently honored during capacity pressure or cross-region failovers. We need a single decision point that consumes account residency settings, allowlist/denylist overrides (both org-level and per-route), service-level tier entitlements, and transient capacity signals to produce a deterministic routing decision and an ordered fallback chain (region + tier + model-variant).

Goals:
- Guarantee that requests from EU-only tenants do not egress to non-EU model hosts under normal operation, and document the narrow, auditable exceptions if a safe escape path is allowed.
- Support allowlist/denylist semantics at tenant, team, and route levels with precedence rules and emergency overrides.
- Produce an ordered fallback plan that prefers same-region compatible model-variants, then same-region lower-tier capacity, then EU-compatible failover region as last resort, while maintaining SLOs for latency and privacy.
- Expose decision reason codes and trace IDs for Console, logs, and billing reconciliation.

Design notes & interfaces:
- Inputs: tenant residency flag (enum: global|eu-only|regional-lock), tenant allowed-regions list, account tier (hosted|dedicated|private), request metadata (headers: X-Customer-Residency, X-Requested-Region), current capacity signals (from CapacityService), and allow/deny overrides from PolicyStore.
- Decision output: route_decision (string), ordered_fallbacks (comma-separated string), reason_code (string), audit_token (trace id). Because our Linear JSON schema forbids nested objects, implementation detail: the switchboard will return a compact flat response to the router.
- Precedence: explicit per-route denylists > tenant denylist > global denylist; explicit per-route allowlist > tenant allowlist > global allowlist. Emergency 'escape' requires two-step approval: automated threshold check + manual operator approval (logged).
- Fallback selection algorithm (high level):
  1) Attempt same-region same-tier compatible model-variant (exact model id or quantized variant).
  2) If unavailable, attempt same-region lower-tier variant (e.g., hosted -> dedicated with burst permissions) if tenant entitlements allow.
  3) If still unavailable and tenant is not eu-only, consider cross-region with strongest data controls.
  4) For eu-only tenants, only allow cross-region fallback to an EU region; if no EU capacity is available, mark as RESERVED and return structured 409 with customer-facing message and operator fallout path.

Operational concerns & telemetry:
- Emit a sampling of decisions to tracing with tags: tenant_id, residency_mode, chosen_route, fallback_chain, capacity_signal, reason_code.
- Console: add a per-tenant 'decision history' panel that surfaces last N decisions and the reason_code.
- Metrics: decision_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), decision_denied_count, escape_approval_count, fallback_usage_by_tier and fallback_usage_by_region.

Security & compliance:
- All switchboard decisions must be auditable and storable in immutable logs (retention configurable by customer).
- Integrate with KMS for signing audit tokens if required by enterprise customers.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement switchboard service behind feature flag; run in shadow mode for 2 weeks for top 50 EU tenants.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable active enforcement for 10% of EU-only tenants; validate SLO/regressions and Console traces.
- Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to full enforcement for all EU-only tenants over 2 weeks, with operator escape workflow enabled but default off.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: decision latency spikes under load. Mitigation: in-memory cache for tenant policies, hot-path compiled policy expressions, and circuit-breaker that falls back to last-known-good decisions.
- Risk: stale allowlist/denylist leading to misrouting. Mitigation: versioned policy objects and last-updated timestamps included in decisions; automatic sync alerts.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the switchboard logic and APIs. Router-side integration and UI components tracked in follow-ups (see links section).
acceptance_criteria: Switchboard returns a decision payload within 5ms p50 and 20ms p95 for 95th percentile of requests in staging
EU-only tenants in canary do not route to non-EU hosts during enforcement runs (verified via audit logs)
Decision payload includes a stable reason_code and audit_token that surface in traces and Console
Emergency escape requires automated threshold + operator approval flow and is logged with operator id
Unit and integration tests cover precedence rules for allowlist/denylist and fallback ordering
comments: 2026-02-21: Initial triage — scoped to switchboard service only. Marcus to prototype policy expression format.
2026-02-28: Design review with PM & Security. Security requested immutable audit log and signed tokens for enterprise customers.
2026-03-04: Prototype implemented in feature branch refs/policy/switchboard-proto. Observed median decision latency ~1.1ms in local benchmark.
2026-03-09: CapacityService contract clarified — will publish availability vectors with region/tier granularity. Added dependency ENG-47211.
2026-03-12: Started shadowing on staging for 30 EU tenants. No misrouted requests detected in 48-hour window. Moving to canary plan next.
Design feedback: PM asked to include tenant-level audit retention toggle and expose escape metrics to SRE dash. Added to acceptance criteria.
